findings.title: Firewall active
findings.evidence:
Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

findings.title: Automatic security updates enabled
findings.evidence: 20auto-upgrades config not found or not enabled

findings.title: No blanket NOPASSWD wildcard in sudoers

fix_list.finding: One or more accounts have an empty password (cis_test_emptypass).
fix_list.why_it_matters: An empty password lets anyone log in as that account with no credential at all.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo passwd -l <account>   # lock each account listed in the evidence, or set a real password

fix_list.finding:
No active default-deny firewall policy was found (Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination).
fix_list.why_it_matters: Without a default-deny firewall policy, every listening service is directly reachable from the network.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo iptables -P INPUT DROP && sudo iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT && sudo iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

fix_list.finding: Root login over SSH is permitted (PermitRootLogin yes).
fix_list.why_it_matters: A leaked or brute-forced root credential grants full remote access with no separate privilege step.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo sed -i 's/^PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl reload sshd

fix_list.finding: SSH password authentication is enabled (PasswordAuthentication yes), allowing brute-force login attempts.
fix_list.why_it_matters: Password auth is vulnerable to brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks; key-based auth removes that attack surface entirely.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo sed -i 's/^PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl reload sshd

fix_list.finding: A blanket NOPASSWD sudoers entry was found (/etc/sudoers.d/90-cis-test-nopasswd:ALL ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL).
fix_list.why_it_matters: A passwordless, unrestricted sudo rule lets anyone with access to that account become root with no additional authentication.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo visudo   # remove the NOPASSWD:ALL line shown in the evidence

fix_list.finding: Automatic security updates are not enabled (20auto-upgrades config not found or not enabled).
fix_list.why_it_matters: Unpatched systems remain exposed to publicly known vulnerabilities long after fixes are available.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo apt-get install -y unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades

fix_list.finding: Minimum password length policy is too weak or unset (PASS_MIN_LEN	5).
fix_list.why_it_matters: Short passwords are far more susceptible to brute-force and dictionary attacks.

fix_list.finding: World-writable files found in sensitive system paths (/etc/cis_test_world_writable).
fix_list.why_it_matters: A world-writable file under /etc or a system bin directory can be modified by any local user to escalate privileges or plant malicious content.
fix_list.fix_command: sudo chmod o-w <file>   # apply to each file path listed in the evidence
